passage: Transcript: Pendulum clocks, and the two things that stopped them being perfect. A pendulum's period is set by its length, and that is the problem, because length is what a metal rod refuses to keep. Warm the room, the rod grows, the bob hangs lower, the clock loses time. The nineteenth-century regulators answered that mechanically. A gridiron pendulum interleaves steel and brass; the brass expands more, and it is mounted so that it lifts the bob by as much as the steel drops it. Riefler went the other way and used a nickel alloy that barely expands at all, so there was almost nothing left to cancel. Now, once temperature was handled the best regulators still wandered, and the wandering tracked the barometer. Air is a fluid. I want you to hear that as two separate claims: a denser atmosphere holds the bob up a little, and it also drags on it, and both of those slow the swing. Hence the tanks. You seal the clock and pump the pressure down. Cotterell argues that the pressure effect was known decades before it was corrected, that observatory logs from the 1860s show clockmakers noticing the correlation and declining to act, because sealing a case puts the escapement beyond the reach of routine maintenance. I would not go that far. The logs record the correlation; I grant him that. Whether anybody read it as a cause, the notes are too thin to say.
prompt: [Academic Talk — Horology] What is the talk mainly about?
choices: Two rival pendulum designs, and the evidence that settled which of them was better
The disagreement over what nineteenth-century clockmakers understood about air pressure
Two successive limits on the accuracy of a pendulum clock, and what was done about each
Why the accuracy of a fine clock came to depend on how well its case was sealed
correct_answer: Two successive limits on the accuracy of a pendulum clock, and what was done about each
explanation: The talk is built in two movements: the rod's expansion and the mechanical answers to it, then the residual drift that tracked the barometer and the sealed tank that answered that. No evidence is ever offered for one pendulum design over the other, so the option about rival designs being settled describes a talk that was not given; the option about the case being sealed promotes the second remedy over the problem it solved; and the option about the disagreement over what clockmakers understood names only the closing minute.

distractor_rationales.choice: Two rival pendulum designs, and the evidence that settled which of them was better
distractor_rationales.reason: The same two-part shape as the key and equally wide, but the talk presents the gridiron and the nickel alloy as two answers to one problem and never adjudicates between them.

distractor_rationales.choice: The disagreement over what nineteenth-century clockmakers understood about air pressure
distractor_rationales.reason: True of the last section only; a candidate who listens to the end and not the start will take the final topic for the whole.

distractor_rationales.choice: Why the accuracy of a fine clock came to depend on how well its case was sealed
distractor_rationales.reason: Promotes one remedy to the thesis, and sealing is the answer to the second limit only.

prompt: [Academic Talk — Horology] According to the professor, what does the brass do in a gridiron pendulum?
choices: It expands more than the steel and is mounted so as to raise the bob
It expands less than the steel and is mounted so as to slow the bob's fall
It carries heat away from the steel so that the steel's own expansion is slowed down
It weights the lower part of the rod so that the swinging length stays where it was set
correct_answer: It expands more than the steel and is mounted so as to raise the bob
explanation: The professor says the brass expands more and is mounted so that it lifts the bob by as much as the steel drops it. The option that has the brass expanding less and slowing the bob's fall reverses the two metals and leaves the error merely delayed; the option about carrying heat away substitutes conduction for expansion; and the option about weighting the lower part of the rod describes a mass effect, where the talk's whole account of the error runs through length.

distractor_rationales.choice: It expands less than the steel and is mounted so as to slow the bob's fall
distractor_rationales.reason: The metals reversed, with the same mounting language as the key so that direction is the only thing separating them.

distractor_rationales.choice: It carries heat away from the steel so that the steel's own expansion is slowed down
distractor_rationales.reason: A different physical mechanism, conduction rather than differential expansion, and one that would delay the error rather than cancel it.

distractor_rationales.choice: It weights the lower part of the rod so that the swinging length stays where it was set
distractor_rationales.reason: Right conclusion, wrong route: the length is indeed held, but by opposed expansions, not by added mass.

prompt: [Academic Talk — Horology] Why does the professor say, 'I want you to hear that as two separate claims'?
choices: To separate the discovery of the effect from the decision to correct it
To distinguish sealing the case from pumping it down, which are done together but for different reasons
To keep the barometer's reading and the clock's own error from being run together
To mark buoyancy and drag as distinct effects that happen to work in the same direction
correct_answer: To mark buoyancy and drag as distinct effects that happen to work in the same direction
explanation: The line is a set-up: he immediately gives two things a denser atmosphere does, holding the bob up and dragging on it, and adds that both slow the swing. The option about separating discovery from correction belongs to the argument he reaches minutes later; the option about sealing and pumping splits a remedy he has not yet named; and the option about keeping the barometer's reading apart from the clock's error inverts the point, since it is their going together that he is explaining.

distractor_rationales.choice: To separate the discovery of the effect from the decision to correct it
distractor_rationales.reason: Names a real distinction in the talk, but one that arrives with the closing argument, not at this line.

distractor_rationales.choice: To distinguish sealing the case from pumping it down, which are done together but for different reasons
distractor_rationales.reason: Two things, as the stem invites, but both are parts of the remedy, which has not been introduced when the line is spoken.

distractor_rationales.choice: To keep the barometer's reading and the clock's own error from being run together
distractor_rationales.reason: Inverts the point: the correlation between the two is the observation he is unpacking, not a confusion he is warning against.

prompt: [Academic Talk — Horology] What does the professor say about the nickel alloy Riefler used?
choices: Its resistance to expansion left a compensating mechanism with little to do
It expanded predictably enough for the resulting error to be calculated in advance
It was adopted after the interleaved design had been found wanting
It lightened the bob, so the pendulum settled faster after any change of length
correct_answer: Its resistance to expansion left a compensating mechanism with little to do
explanation: The professor says the alloy barely expands at all, so there was almost nothing left to cancel. The option about expansion being predictable enough to calculate substitutes correction on paper for the physical cancelling the talk describes; the option about the interleaved design being found wanting supplies a verdict between the two approaches that is never given; and the option about lightening the bob puts the account back on mass, where the whole explanation of the error runs through length.

distractor_rationales.choice: It expanded predictably enough for the resulting error to be calculated in advance
distractor_rationales.reason: Replaces a mechanical remedy with an arithmetic one; a plausible answer to thermal drift that the talk does not give.

distractor_rationales.choice: It was adopted after the interleaved design had been found wanting
distractor_rationales.reason: Invents a succession. Riefler is introduced as going the other way, not as correcting a failure.

distractor_rationales.choice: It lightened the bob, so the pendulum settled faster after any change of length
distractor_rationales.reason: A mass effect where the talk's account is dimensional, and 'settling faster' is not accuracy.

prompt: [Academic Talk — Horology] What does the professor imply about the observatory logs of the 1860s?
choices: That Cotterell has found in them a correlation they do not actually record
That they record the correlation but not what anyone at the time took it to mean
That they record the correlation and show it being read as a nuisance rather than a cause
That they record the correlation, and that sealing a case cost too much to act on it
correct_answer: That they record the correlation but not what anyone at the time took it to mean
explanation: He grants Cotterell the correlation outright and withholds only the reading of it, saying the notes are too thin to show whether anyone took it as a cause. The option denying that the logs record a correlation refuses more than he refuses; the option that has the effect read as a nuisance supplies exactly the interpretation he says the notes cannot support; and the option about sealing a case costing too much is Cotterell's own explanation, the part of the account he answers with 'I would not go that far'.

distractor_rationales.choice: That Cotterell has found in them a correlation they do not actually record
distractor_rationales.reason: Over-refusal. He concedes the correlation is on the page and disputes only its interpretation.

distractor_rationales.choice: That they record the correlation and show it being read as a nuisance rather than a cause
distractor_rationales.reason: Concedes and qualifies in the same shape as the key, but fills in a reading he says the notes are too thin to supply.

distractor_rationales.choice: That they record the correlation, and that sealing a case cost too much to act on it
distractor_rationales.reason: Cotterell's own claim, restated. It is the part the professor declines to go along with, so it cannot be what he implies.
